ambiguities.clauseRef: 80% of net after expenses. Expenses capped $550.
ambiguities.description: 'After expenses' could mean (a) after actual expenses up to the $550 cap — i.e., if actuals are $400, artist gets 80% of gross minus $400 — or (b) always after the full $550 cap regardless of actual spend. These produce different artist payouts when actuals fall below the cap.

plausibleReadings.summary: Artist pays actual expenses up to the $550 ceiling; if actuals are lower, artist benefits.
plausibleReadings.impact: Artist-favorable when actuals < $550. E.g., if actuals are $300, artist gets 80% of (gross − $300) instead of 80% of (gross − $550), a difference of $200 × 0.80 = $160.

plausibleReadings.summary: The $550 cap is always the deduction regardless of actual spend; venue keeps any savings below the cap.
plausibleReadings.impact: Venue-favorable when actuals < $550. On a show where actuals are $300, venue retains an extra $160 that would otherwise go to artist.

ambiguities.suggestedClarification: When actuals come in below the $550 cap, do we net against actual expenses or always deduct the full $550? Can you confirm which applies here?

sourceText: 80% of net after expenses. Expenses capped $550. No guarantee.
